names.name: Sukhāvatī, the Pure Land of Peace and Bliss (Anle, Anyang, Jile)
the uncreated dharma-body of true wisdom (zhenshi zhihui wuwei fashen)

descriptions: The three adornments of the land, the Buddha and the bodhisattvas 'enter the one dharma-phrase': the pure phrase, which is the uncreated dharma-body of true wisdom (Rebirth Treatise, T1524 232b22-25).
The Pure Land surpasses the paths of the three realms, is ultimately like space, vast and boundless (T1524 230c21-22); it is not included in the three realms (Tanluan, Daochuo).
Amitābha now present is a reward-body buddha and his land a reward land (Daochuo, Anle ji 5c; Shandao).
The dharma-body of dharma-nature gives rise to the dharma-body of expedient means and the latter manifests the former; different but inseparable, one but not identical (Tanluan's Commentary).
negations: Birth there is 'the birth of non-birth', not the deluded birth of the three existences (T1958 11c11-14).
The Buddha seen in samādhi neither comes nor goes; mind makes the buddha (Pratyutpanna; Contemplation Sūtra 8).
relation_to_self: Beings are ordinary foolish beings bound by passions (fanfu) who cannot reach awakening by their own power in this age; they are embraced by the Buddha's light and vow; in the Chan-inflected reading, 'this mind is the Buddha' and Amitābha is the Buddha of one's own nature, but birth in the West is still to be sought.
relation_to_world: This Sahā world of five turbidities is to be loathed and left; Sukhāvatī, created by Dharmākara's vows, lies west beyond ten trillion buddha-lands; for the mind-only reading the pure land is where the mind is pure, without denying the Western land.
caveat: Pure Land teachers insist on the distinctness of Amitābha and his land from the practitioner ('pointing to a direction and establishing form') and would reject a reading that dissolves the Western land into a symbol of one truth; they accept the Mahāyāna identity of all buddhas in dharma-nature but hold that one must rely on this Buddha's vow. The equation of Amitābha with a single ultimate is therefore made only in the interpretation layer and only under P1-level.

names.name: Gokuraku jōdo (the Land of Utmost Bliss)
the name Namu Amida Butsu, in which all virtues are gathered

descriptions: The name contains all the virtues of the Buddha's inner realization and outer activity; hence it is superior and was selected in the primal vow (Senchakushū 3).
Amida is a reward-body buddha in a reward land to which ordinary beings are born by the power of the vow (following Shandao).
relation_to_self: The practitioner is an ignorant ordinary being who should, like one who knows not a single letter, simply say the nenbutsu (One-Sheet Document).
relation_to_world: This world in the last age is to be left; the Pure Land in the west is where awakening is completed; one lives so as best to say the nenbutsu.
caveat: Jōdo-shū keeps 'pointing to a direction and establishing form' (shihō rissō) and rejects readings of the Pure Land as mind only; it would not accept reducing Amida to an impersonal absolute.

names.name: Amida Nyorai; the Tathāgata of Unhindered Light filling the ten directions (Jin jippō mugekō nyorai)

descriptions: The supreme Buddha is formless; being formless it is called jinen; Amida is the means by which we are made to know jinen (the jinen hōni letter).
The true Buddha is the Tathāgata of inconceivable light; the true land is the land of immeasurable light (Kyōgyōshinshō, chapter on the true Buddha and land).
Shinjin is buddha-nature; buddha-nature is the Tathāgata (Jōdo wasan; Kyōgyōshinshō, Shin chapter).
negations: Birth is not attained by the practitioner's calculation (hakarai); 'no working is true working'.
relation_to_self: The self is a foolish being full of blind passions for whom no practice is possible; shinjin, given by Amida, is itself the Buddha's mind in the person, who becomes 'equal to the Tathāgatas' while remaining a foolish being.
relation_to_world: The world is a burning house where 'all is empty and false; only the nenbutsu is true' (Tannishō postscript); one returns to it from the Pure Land to save others (gensō).
caveat: Shinshū distinguishes sharply between the Buddha's mind and the foolish being's mind, and between the true and transformed lands; it would reject any reading that makes the practitioner already a buddha by his own realization or that treats Amida as one deity among many worthy of worship.

names.name: the name Namu Amida Butsu (as itself birth)

descriptions: The birth of all beings was settled as 'Namu Amida Butsu' at Amida's perfect awakening ten kalpas ago (Kumano oracle, as reported in the Ippen Hijiri-e).
In the nenbutsu the self, the Buddha and the name are not separate; the name recites the name (reported sayings).
relation_to_self: The self is to be cast off; not even faith is to be relied on as one's own.
relation_to_world: Everything — mountains, rivers, grasses, the sound of wind and waves — is the nenbutsu (reported sayings, Goroku).
caveat: Ippen's sayings survive mainly in later compilations; the view is reconstructed from them (low confidence on wording).

descriptions: One and all interfuse: one person's recitation contains all persons' and all practices (revelation verse).
relation_to_self: Each practitioner's nenbutsu is shared with all others through interfusion.
relation_to_world: Birth by other-power is realised through the interfusion of all beings' recitation.
caveat: Reconstructed from the revelation verse as transmitted; the school's later doctrinal writings were not consulted (low confidence).

names.name: Amitābha and the Western Land, read through the Tiantai 'four lands'

descriptions: Mao Ziyuan taught the 'perfect interfusion of the four lands and three contemplations' (Lushan lianzong baojian).
relation_to_self: The lay practitioner keeps the five precepts and recites to purify the five roots.
relation_to_world: The five turbidities of this world are to be left through the five precepts and recitation.
caveat: Known only through its defender Pudu's compilation; views of the later White Lotus sects are not represented here.
